title: Respiratory supplied key report — archive labelled August 2026
note: All six photographed report pages were manually checked. They contain Q1–38 and asterisks marking one supplied answer per question. Photographs show August 15, 2026 timestamps; no exam date or authenticated official-key status is established. Spelling and grammar are lightly normalized with substantive repairs documented.

questions.prompt: Which lung volume cannot be measured by spirometry?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Residual volume cannot be exhaled into a spirometer; capacities containing it also require another measurement method.

questions.prompt: Which muscle plays a key role during inspiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The diaphragm is the main muscle of quiet inspiration. Scalenes may assist inspiration; the wording 'key role' is interpreted as principal rather than exclusive.

questions.prompt: Under normal conditions, which compartment has negative pressure?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Pleural pressure is normally subatmospheric during quiet spontaneous breathing. Airway pressures vary with airflow, whereas the pleural space is the intended persistently negative compartment.

questions.prompt: Which is not part of anatomical dead space?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Gas-exchanging alveoli are outside anatomical conducting dead space. Unperfused alveoli can contribute alveolar dead space, a separate concept.

questions.prompt: Which factor shifts the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve to the right?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Increased CO2 lowers oxygen affinity and shifts the curve right. The other listed changes favor a left shift.

questions.prompt: What is the principal mechanism by which oxygen is transported in blood?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Most blood oxygen is reversibly bound to hemoglobin; only a small fraction is physically dissolved under normal conditions.

questions.prompt: What is the principal mechanism by which CO2 is transported in blood?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Most CO2 is transported after conversion to bicarbonate; carbamino and dissolved forms account for smaller fractions.

questions.prompt: In spirometry, measurement of which volume requires maximal effort?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Inspiratory reserve volume requires a maximal inspiration after an ordinary inspiration. FRC and RV cannot be measured directly by simple spirometry.

questions.prompt: Which is a non-respiratory function of the respiratory system?
options: Transport of CO2 from tissues to lungs
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Pulmonary endothelial ACE converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II, an endocrine/metabolic function of the lung.

questions.prompt: In which region of the lung is physiological dead space present?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The supplied answer C appears to mean the increased high-V/Q alveolar-dead-space contribution at the apex. Physiological dead space also includes conducting anatomical dead space throughout the lungs, so the printed question is not uniquely answered by C. Held ungraded rather than silently replacing physiological with alveolar.

questions.prompt: In which region of the lung is alveolar ventilation less than perfusion?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the upright lung the basal V/Q ratio is lower than one; apical V/Q is higher because perfusion falls more than ventilation.

questions.prompt: Which part of the respiratory tree belongs to the conducting zone?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Bronchi conduct air without alveolar exchange surfaces. Respiratory bronchioles, alveolar ducts and sacs belong to the respiratory region.

questions.prompt: Which structure is inactive during quiet normal inspiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The source marks A, reflecting the older simplified description of the VRG as recruited during forceful breathing. It is too absolute: inspiratory neurons in the ventral respiratory column participate in quiet breathing. DRG and diaphragm are active, so no literally correct option is available.

questions.prompt: Which center is responsible for the inspiratory switch-off signal?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Pontine pneumotaxic-region input limits inspiratory duration in the classic center model.

questions.prompt: What is the direct stimulus for the chemosensitive area?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Local H+ directly excites central chemosensitive neurons; CO2 is a powerful indirect stimulus because it enters brain fluids and produces H+.

questions.prompt: In an environment with high oxygen concentration, what happens?
options: There is no change in oxygen binding or release
Oxygen binding and release rates remain in equilibrium
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Higher PO2 favors hemoglobin oxygen loading, provided binding sites remain available. This describes the shift after exposure, not the final equilibrium state.

questions.prompt: Which factor increases lung compliance?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Surfactant lowers alveolar surface tension, reducing recoil and the pressure needed for expansion.

questions.prompt: Which finding indicates an obstructive ventilatory pattern?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Airflow obstruction lowers FEV1 disproportionately relative to vital capacity, decreasing the ratio. The ratio alone does not establish a disease-specific diagnosis.

questions.prompt: Which molecule binds at the same hemoglobin site as oxygen?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO binds heme iron at the oxygen-binding site; CO2 binds amino groups rather than that heme site.

questions.prompt: In which environment is oxygen partial pressure greatest?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: For ordinary room air at sea level, dry atmospheric PO2 exceeds alveolar and blood PO2. This assumes the same ambient conditions and no supplemental oxygen.

questions.prompt: Which respiratory center is active during forced expiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Expiratory neurons of the ventral respiratory group provide drive to expiratory muscles during increased ventilatory demand.

questions.prompt: In which compartment is CO2 partial pressure highest?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the resting textbook comparison, metabolically active tissue cells have slightly higher PCO2 than venous/interstitial blood, and both exceed alveolar/arterial PCO2.

questions.prompt: In which microscopic tissue are bipolar neurons observed?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Olfactory receptor cells are bipolar neurons in the olfactory epithelium.

questions.prompt: In which part of the respiratory air duct is a bundle of elastic fibers observed?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: C is the supplied mark, likely alluding to the elastic vocal ligament. The stem does not specify that structure, and bronchial walls also contain elastic fibers; the broad location question does not establish a unique answer.

questions.prompt: Which part of a lung lobule has simple cuboidal epithelial tissue?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Both terminal/small bronchioles (included in B) and respiratory bronchioles (C) have simple cuboidal epithelial portions. These overlapping options make the source's C non-unique.

questions.prompt: Where in the microscopic structure of the lung are pneumocytes type III observed?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The scan clearly says pneumocytes type III and marks A. Type III is nonstandard and has been used inconsistently; if the author meant dust cells, A is plausible, but macrophages are not type I/II epithelial pneumocytes. The undefined terminology prevents a defensible single key.

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles are innervated by the recurrent laryngeal nerve except:
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Cricothyroid receives the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve; the other listed intrinsic muscles receive recurrent laryngeal supply.

questions.prompt: At the midclavicular line, at which rib is the inferior border of the lung?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The inferior lung margin reaches approximately rib 6 in the midclavicular line; the pleural reflection lies around rib 8.

questions.prompt: All of the following are found in the middle meatus except:
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus.

questions.prompt: Where is the uncinate process found?
options: In the medial wall of the nasal cavity
On the inferior surface of the ethmoidal labyrinth
In the cribriform plate of the ethmoid
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The uncinate process arises from the ethmoidal labyrinth and projects into the lateral nasal wall near the middle meatus.

questions.prompt: A patient has frequent severe epistaxis from the anterior-inferior nasal septum. Which artery is not responsible for this bleeding?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The other listed arteries contribute septal branches to the anterior septal anastomosis. External nasal supply primarily serves the external nose; the expected additional septal contributor is the anterior ethmoidal artery.

questions.prompt: Which bone contributes to both the roof and lateral wall of the nasal cavity?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The ethmoid contributes its cribriform plate to the roof and its labyrinth/conchae to the lateral wall.

questions.prompt: Which muscle attaches to the anterior surface of the pyramidal (arytenoid) cartilage?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Vocalis/medial thyroarytenoid attaches at the anterior vocal-process region. Posterior cricoarytenoid uses the muscular process, and the arytenoid muscles lie posteriorly.

questions.prompt: The quadrangular membrane attaches to all of the following except:
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The quadrangular membrane extends between epiglottic/thyroid and arytenoid regions; cricoid is associated with the conus elasticus below.

questions.prompt: Which nerve passes through the incisive canal?
options: External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The nasopalatine nerve passes through the incisive canal toward the anterior hard palate.

questions.prompt: Which nerve passes through an opening in the thyrohyoid membrane?
options: Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The internal laryngeal nerve pierces the thyrohyoid membrane with the superior laryngeal vessels.

questions.prompt: All of the following statements are correct except:
options: The azygos vein is adjacent to the medial surface of the right lung
The visceral pleura is innervated by the phrenic nerve
The lung apex is at the root of the neck
The pulmonary vein is the most anterior element in the left lung hilum
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The phrenic nerve supplies mediastinal and central diaphragmatic parietal pleura, not visceral pleura. Source 'umbilicus' is normalized to hilum in option D.

questions.prompt: All of the following attach to the thyroid cartilage except:
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The aryepiglottic fold extends from the epiglottis to the arytenoid region. Vocal and vestibular structures attach anteriorly to thyroid cartilage, and thyropharyngeus originates from its oblique line. The source stem ends with the nonsensical words 'the and the calyx'; those words are omitted without changing the anatomical question.

notes: All 6 pages and all 38 visible MCQs accounted for; no cover, Q39 or Q40 is present. No absent questions were invented.
All 38 supplied asterisk marks preserved. Audited keys withheld for Q10, Q13, Q24, Q25 and Q26.
